title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
authors: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Joan Elias Miro
abstract: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework for a 2+1 dimensional superfluid model coupled to a CFT, demonstrating that the system can maintain superfluid order (BKT phase) even at very high temperatures. By constructing and analyzing a reduced 2D effective field theory, the authors determine the phase boundary by matching their continuum results to known lattice critical points.
main_problem: The paper investigates constructing a UV-complete model in 2+1 dimensions that sustains a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase even at arbitrarily high temperatures, challenging typical expectations of thermal disorder.
main_result: The analysis shows that the system can exhibit a reentrant BKT superfluidity sequence at high temperatures, driven by the asymptotic dominance of the CFT contribution in the effective field theory.
method: The approach involves deriving a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory by separating scales and integrating out static screening modes, followed by matching this theory to lattice Monte Carlo results.
model_or_system: The model is a complex scalar field $\chi$ in $d=2+1$ dimensions coupled to a Conformal Field Theory (CFT) via a portal interaction. The analysis also references lattice models of the XY model and the general framework of superfluid phase transitions.
key_observables: Phase stiffness ($K$), correlation decay (algebraic vs. exponential), and the critical surface $R_c$ that separates different superfluid regimes.
important_parameters: The portal coupling $h$, the CFT operator dimension $\Delta$, and the temperature $T$. The critical value $R_c = -0.821(10)$ is crucial.
main_assumptions: Assumes small couplings ($\lambda \ll 1$) and that the analysis is controlled in the window $1 < \Delta < 3/2$ to ensure vacuum stability and controlled backreaction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate representative trajectories in the phase diagram ($\delta_{	ext{rep}}U(1)+	ext{CFT}(t)$ vs. $\log(T/m)$), showing the crossing of the critical surface $\delta(T)=0$ which marks the transition between superfluid phases.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the UV-complete model and its effective action, through the scale separation and derivation of the 2D effective theory, to determining the phase boundary by matching continuum theory results to established lattice Monte Carlo critical values.
why_interesting: The investigation of high-temperature superfluidity via CFT coupling provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding exotic phase transitions in quantum matter, relevant to both condensed matter and quantum field theory.
